## What does the public benefit label promise?

- **PBCs must balance three interests.** Under Delaware law a public benefit corporation's directors must balance stockholders, those materially affected by its conduct, and the public benefit its charter names. `[A001 | 1 | Q007]`
- **The charter names the benefit.** Anthropic's certificate of incorporation says its specific public benefit is to responsibly develop and maintain advanced AI for the long term benefit of humanity. `[A002 | 1 | Q095]`
- **The label is a promise.** So the public benefit corporation label is a promise: the company is built, at its core, to do what it says. `[A003 | 1 | A001, A002]`
- **Five pillars, no metrics.** The board has adopted five pillars, each describing a world where AI has gone well, as conditions rather than metrics. `[A004 | 1 | Q002]`
- **Report and S-1 describe the Fund differently.** The Report calls the 5% Public Benefit Fund a plan subject to stockholder approval; the S-1 records the shares as contributed to a wholly owned subsidiary. `[A005 | 1 | Q003, Q004, Q006]`
- **Separate in law, not in control.** A wholly owned subsidiary is a separate entity in law but not in control, so investors should price the S-1 version. `[A006 | 1 | A005, Q005]`
- **Scrutiny runs backwards.** A small benefit whose worst case is that nothing good happens is checked end to end; Anthropic is checked by its own report. `[A007 | 0 | Q034, P-woodcache]`
- **The promise is worth checking.** Therefore the promise is worth checking. `[A008 | 0 | A003, A007]`

## What is Anthropic's best case?

- **Directors need not maximise value.** A Delaware court has held that a public benefit corporation's directors need not maximise shareholder value. `[A009 | 0 | P-drakes-landing]`
- **A trust elects four of seven.** An independent trust, the Long-Term Benefit Trust, elects four of Anthropic's seven directors. `[A010 | 0 | P-s1-ltbt]`
- **It discloses its own failures.** Anthropic discloses its models' risks, including its own failures, such as four models reaching real third-party systems in testing. `[A011 | 1 | Q094, Q067, Q041a, Q041b]`
- **It discloses more than peers.** Anthropic discloses more about its models' risks than its peers do. `[A012 | 0 | P-peer-disclosure]`
- **The Constitution is public.** Anthropic published its model's Constitution openly, under CC0, a public-domain dedication. `[A013 | 0 | P-constitution-cc0]`
- **Outcomes take time.** Its own trust reads this first report as largely describing inputs and says it will look for outcomes in later reports. `[A014 | 1 | Q034]`
- **The best case is strong.** Anthropic's best case that it keeps the promise is strong: a chartered purpose, a court ruling that directors need not maximise value, a trust-elected board majority, and leading disclosure. `[A015 | 0 | A002, A009, A010, A011, A012]`
- **The arrow is unearned.** The case fails not on aims but on one inference: inputs plus intentions plus revocable trustees equals a discharged public duty. `[A016 | 0 | A015, A014]`

## Who can make Anthropic keep the promise?

- **No duty to any person.** DGCL §365(b) gives directors no duty to any person on account of a public-benefit interest. `[A017 | 0 | P-dgcl-365b]`
- **Only 2% holders may sue.** Only holders of 2%, or once listed the lesser of 2% and $2 million, may sue derivatively to enforce the purpose (§367). `[A018 | 0 | P-dgcl-367]`
- **The public cannot enforce it.** The public the charter names cannot enforce it. `[A019 | 0 | A017, A018]`
- **The lock is untested.** The S-1 warns that no judicial precedent interprets the structure, which increases the risk and unpredictability of governance litigation. `[A020 | 1 | Q011]`
- **Founders hold 50.1%.** Seven co-founders control 50.1% of the general vote through a single Class F share held by Founder LLC. `[A021 | 0 | P-s1-classf]`
- **The trust is revocable.** The trust's Class T can be amended away by the shareholder classes it is meant to check. `[A022 | 0 | P-trust-agreement]`
- **Only at the frontier.** The S-1 says safety requires research at the frontier, and that the business model needs increasing capital to stay there. `[A023 | 0 | Q012, Q013, Q017]`
- **Restraint is industry-wide.** Its call to pace the frontier is for industry-wide standards and, the S-1 says, does not describe its own release timelines. `[A024 | 1 | Q015, Q016]`
- **The RSP delays only in the lead.** The RSP binds delay only while Anthropic holds a significant lead; otherwise it commits to try to match better mitigations, not to delay. `[A025 | 0 | Q019, Q020, Q021, Q022a, Q022b]`
- **The RSP allows caution.** In fairness, the RSP says its commitments do not preclude cautionary action, and Anthropic would strongly consider pausing in cases it does not cover. `[A026 | 1 | Q023, Q024]`
- **Considering is not committing.** Considering a pause is not a commitment: the binding delay is still conditioned on holding the lead or on a competitor's better mitigation. `[A027 | 0 | A025, A026]`
- **Only we can save us.** Read together: hold back while in the lead, otherwise keep pace. That is only-we-can-save-us written as policy. `[A028 | 0 | A023, A024, A027]`
- **Governance depends on the few.** If only a few people can steer this technology safely, the governance must survive them; this one depends on them. `[A029 | 0 | A021, A022, A028]`
- **The promise rests on its word.** So the promise rests on Anthropic's word. `[A030 | 0 | A019, A020, A029]`

## By what standard do we check its word?

- **Two unverifiable agents.** Anthropic manages a Claude it cannot fully verify; the public has to manage an Anthropic it cannot fully verify. `[A031 | 0 | Q065, A030]`
- **The Constitution is the authority.** Anthropic calls its Constitution the final authority on its vision for Claude. `[A032 | 0 | Q025]`
- **A lens, not a rule.** We read the Constitution as a lens on how Anthropic governs an agent it cannot verify, not as a rule that binds Anthropic. `[A033 | 0 | A031, A032]`
- **Safety and ethics first.** The Constitution ranks broad safety, then ethics, then Anthropic's guidelines, then helpfulness, holistically rather than strictly; we score in that order. `[A034 | 0 | Q026a, Q026b]`
- **Selective emphasis is deception.** The Constitution counts selective emphasis, technically true statements and deceptive framing as ways of creating false impressions. `[A035 | 0 | Q027]`
- **Concealment for advantage.** The Constitution counts concealing material risk information for advantage as illegitimate power-seeking, so applying it to Anthropic requires concealment, not mere pursuit of advantage. `[A036 | 0 | Q028, Q029]`
- **No exemption for its maker.** The Constitution tells Claude to refuse illegitimate power concentration even when Anthropic asks, and names Anthropic among possible illegitimate seizers. `[A037 | 0 | Q030, Q031]`

## What does the record show?

- **Inputs reported as outcomes.** Dashboards flagging 25,000 pneumonia cases are an input; cases averted would be an outcome. The Report admits it has not collected enough data. `[A038 | 1 | Q083, Q038]`
- **Claude grades Claude.** The 80% productivity figure is Claude estimating Claude's own effect on task time. `[A039 | 0 | Q084]`
- **Security counts are unaudited.** The flagship count of more than 33,000 critical- and high-severity flaws has no public CVE-level audit. `[A040 | 0 | Q081, P-cve-audit]`
- **Its emphasis would count as deception.** By the standard Anthropic set for Claude, the Report's selective emphasis would count as deception: it reports inputs as outcomes and grades itself. `[A041 | 0 | A033, A035, A014, A038, A039]`
- **Bartz: a priced harm.** Anthropic settled Bartz for $1.5 billion over pirated books and excludes the settlement from its adjusted operating income. `[A042 | 0 | Q039a, P-bartz]`
- **Revenue from policy violators.** The S-1 estimates 5–7% of nine-month 2026 revenue came from customers later found violating its usage policy. `[A043 | 0 | P-s1-violator-revenue]`
- **Models escaped in testing.** Four of its models gained unauthorized access to real third-party systems in testing. `[A044 | 1 | Q094]`
- **Misuse disrupted after the fact.** In one disrupted extortion operation, the actor targeted at least 17 distinct organisations. `[A045 | 0 | Q048]`
- **Benefit: binding, not medicine.** At the same standard of proof, the benefit is protein binding confirmed in independent labs: no neutralisation and no medicine. `[A046 | 0 | Q080, P-binder-confirmation]`
- **Harms documented, benefits anecdote.** On a like-for-like standard of proof, its harms are documented and priced; its benefits are mostly anecdote. `[A047 | 0 | A042, A043, A044, A045, A046, A038, A039]`
- **A settlement is not consent.** A settlement pays for a car accident; it does not staff the intersection. Payment for one taking is not a licence for the rest. `[A048 | 0 | A042]`
- **Gains claimed, harms returned.** Harms are returned to the power-intensive nature of the industry and to public perception of job displacement, regardless of actual impact. `[A049 | 1 | Q042, Q043, Q044]`
- **Restraint is voluntary.** No mandatory independent check exists on whether frontier labs follow their safety policies, and the White House Accord carries no penalties. `[A050 | 1 | Q045, Q069c]`
- **A forecast is not an offset.** A hoped 20% of shares to the public good is a forecast, counted now against harms already settled in cash. `[A051 | 1 | Q089]`
- **Exposure is disclosed.** Systemic risk needs no body count: $895.4 billion of committed spend and decisions concentrated among a few, with few external checks, are disclosed. `[A052 | 1 | Q090, Q073a, Q073b]`
- **Acts where leverage is weakest.** Anthropic acts at the low-leverage end, numbers and information flows, and leaves the high-leverage rules and structure with the governed. `[A053 | 0 | A011, A019, A021, A022]`
- **No seat for those extracted from.** Host communities, data workers and corpus authors hold no seat, vote or standing in its governance. `[A054 | 0 | A019, A021, A022]`
- **Use is concentrated.** AI use is heavily concentrated in wealthier countries, and Anthropic is not yet able to host Claude locally everywhere. `[A055 | 0 | Q049, Q050]`

## Does each pillar meet its own standard?

- **Pillar 1: safety is not solved.** Pillar 1 says safety's technical problems are solved; the Report says alignment is far from solved and flaws may surface only after an incident. `[A056 | 0 | Q061, Q055, Q066]`
- **Pillar 2: no law backstops it.** Pillar 2 says safety is backstopped by law; Congress has enacted no federal framework, and labs largely run on voluntary commitments. `[A057 | 1 | Q068, Q069a, Q069b]`
- **Pillar 3: control is concentrated.** Pillar 3 says no single actor controls the future; the Report says a handful, Anthropic among them, decide, creating a significant power imbalance. `[A058 | 1 | Q071, Q072, Q073a, Q073b, Q073d]`
- **Pillar 4: impacts are unknown.** Pillar 4 promises prosperity; the Report says impacts on workers are still mostly unknown and gains may accrue mainly to large businesses. `[A059 | 1 | Q074, Q075a, Q075b]`
- **Pillar 5: benefits are not shared.** Pillar 5 says benefits are shared by everyone; use is concentrated in wealthier countries. `[A060 | 0 | Q077, A055]`
- **Each pillar meets its own counterpoint.** For every pillar, Anthropic's own text supplies the counterpoint: the condition is a world it hopes for, and its admissions say it has not arrived. `[A079 | 0 | A056, A057, A058, A059, A060]`

## Can the planet tolerate this buildout?

*Lens: planetary-boundaries. Other lenses in the deck: remaining-carbon-budget, doughnut, local-basin, energy-abundance.*

- **Every lens is a test; none can run.** Each lens yields a test of the buildout, but none can be run on Anthropic until it publishes metered energy, water and emissions figures, which the S-1 extract lacks. `[A061 | 0 | L-planet-planetary-boundaries-12, L-planet-remaining-carbon-budget-04, L-planet-doughnut-03, L-planet-local-basin-05, L-planet-energy-abundance-04, L-planet-local-basin-04]`
- **The load is measured globally.** Data centres used about 415 TWh of electricity in 2024, and their electricity emissions are about 180 Mt today, per the IEA. `[A062 | 1 | Q114, Q113]`
- **Boundaries define a safe space.** Planetary boundaries are proposed limits on Earth-system processes within which humanity is expected to operate safely. `[L-planet-planetary-boundaries-01 | 1 | Q097]`
- **A boundary embeds a judgement.** Where a boundary sits is not pure science: choosing its safe distance from a threshold involves normative judgements about risk. `[L-planet-planetary-boundaries-02 | 1 | Q098]`
- **Two boundaries a data centre touches.** Data centres draw on the climate boundary (CO2 below 350 ppm) and the freshwater boundary (under 4000 km3 a year of consumptive use). `[L-planet-planetary-boundaries-03 | 1 | L-planet-planetary-boundaries-01, Q099, Q100]`
- **No unique compute budget.** Boundaries supply no unique compute budget: turning a global limit into a sector, operator or site share needs explicit assumptions and a distributive choice. `[L-planet-planetary-boundaries-04 | 1 | L-planet-planetary-boundaries-02, Q102]`
- **Allocate: equal per capita.** Equal per capita: every person gets the same share of the safe operating space, whatever they use today. `[L-planet-planetary-boundaries-05 | 0 | L-planet-planetary-boundaries-03, P-bjorn-2020]` Alternatives: L-planet-planetary-boundaries-06, L-planet-planetary-boundaries-07.
- **Downscale to the sector.** The sector share s_sector, the fraction of an allocated allowance spent on computing, is a second choice no boundary paper sets; it is open here. `[L-planet-planetary-boundaries-08 | 0 | L-planet-planetary-boundaries-05]`
- **Downscale to the operator.** The operator share s_op splits the sector's allowance by market share, service delivered, or another stated rule; each rule gives a different number. `[L-planet-planetary-boundaries-09 | 0 | L-planet-planetary-boundaries-08]`
- **Energy budget formula.** E_op = B × s_sector × s_op ÷ I_grid: allocated remaining CO2 over grid emission intensity. Assumes the climate boundary is read as a cumulative budget; all inputs open. `[L-planet-planetary-boundaries-10 | 0 | L-planet-planetary-boundaries-09, L-planet-remaining-carbon-budget-01]`
- **Water budget formula.** W_op = W_basin,season × s_op: the basin's sustainable consumptive allowance, not the global 4000 km3, sets it. Inputs open until basin data are pinned. `[L-planet-planetary-boundaries-11 | 0 | L-planet-planetary-boundaries-09, Q100, L-planet-local-basin-01]`
- **The budget follows once a rule is chosen.** The objection holds only until a rule is chosen: with an allocation principle and both shares stated, the budget is arithmetic and every assumption is contestable. `[L-planet-planetary-boundaries-12 | 0 | L-planet-planetary-boundaries-04, L-planet-planetary-boundaries-10, L-planet-planetary-boundaries-11]`
- **Compute is downstream.** A compute budget is E_op times useful compute per kWh, bounded by W_op too; a scalar FLOP cap hides which limit binds. `[L-planet-planetary-boundaries-13 | 0 | L-planet-planetary-boundaries-10, L-planet-planetary-boundaries-11]`
- **The values are rough.** The boundary values are rough first estimates with large uncertainties, so any budget derived from them inherits that uncertainty. `[L-planet-planetary-boundaries-14 | 1 | Q101]`
- **The 2023 update is unpinned.** A 2023 update re-quantified all nine boundaries; its findings stay out of these cards until it is pinned. `[L-planet-planetary-boundaries-15 | 0 | P-richardson-2023]`

## What is the answer?

- **PBC in law, not in sense.** Anthropic is a public benefit corporation in law, not in the sense the category promises: no one it names can make it act like one. `[A063 | 0 | A008, A030, A041, A047]`

## What would governance that binds look like?

- **Governance others can invoke.** The remedy is not a better report but governance that someone Anthropic does not appoint, pay or outvote can invoke. `[A064 | 0 | A063, A048]`
- **Irrevocable mission lock.** The decisive mechanism is an irrevocable mission lock: Class T votes, or a golden veto, held by a purpose trust with an enforcer. `[A065 | 0 | A022]`
- **Contest standing.** Cure §365 and §367 by charter: give affected people standing to contest a use, with equal visibility. `[A066 | 0 | A019]`
- **Metered externality bond.** Meter site power, water and displacement against a bond that forfeits on breach, with deadlines for incident disclosure. `[A067 | 0 | L-planet-local-basin-04]`
- **Pre-IPO asks.** Before pricing: file the Trust Agreement terms, dollarise the 5–7%, publish site power and water, make the Fund independent, restate benefit numbers. `[A068 | 0 | A064, A065, A043, A067, A006, A040]`
- **Praxis builds the other half.** Praxis makes the demands running code: a byte-exact verifier anyone can re-run, with no trusted intermediary, us included. `[A069 | 0 | A064, P-descartes-state]`

## What would change our mind?

- **What levers exist?.** The governing question is what levers an affected community has to push back; for those the paper names, today close to none. `[A070 | 0 | A054, A019]`
- **Falsifier: audited security counts.** We amend the verdict if Anthropic publishes CVE-level, deduplicated, externally attested security-benefit counts. `[A071 | 0 | A063]`
- **Falsifier: outcome evaluations.** We amend the verdict if Anthropic publishes outcome evaluations, not dashboards, from WHO-class partners. `[A072 | 0 | A063]`
- **Falsifier: corpus provenance.** We amend the verdict if Anthropic publishes an audited corpus-provenance percentage with an operating rights-holder exit. `[A073 | 0 | A063]`
- **Falsifier: misuse dollars.** We amend the verdict if quarterly misuse-revenue dollars trend under 1%, with victim counts. `[A074 | 0 | A063]`
- **Falsifier: irrevocable lock.** We amend the verdict if Anthropic adopts an irrevocable charter amendment implementing the mission lock. `[A075 | 0 | A063, A065]`
- **Falsifier: metered sites.** We amend the verdict if Anthropic publishes metered site footprints; that also lets the planet lenses run. `[A076 | 0 | A063, A067]`
- **Our standing.** This is sponsor-side analysis by an adviser building a competing governance tool; no affected person was interviewed. `[A077 | 0 | P-sloane-standing]`
- **The lens cuts both ways.** Praxis is held to the same test: Descartes is single-machine with no contest relation yet, so it transfers as design, not deployed proof. `[A078 | 0 | P-descartes-state, A033]`
